evals.prompt: The report export specification is approved and its five tasks are listed in task-graph.md. Please implement the whole batch, in parallel where you can, and keep the cost reasonable.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the agreement and graph, builds a routing table, and stops for approval before dispatching any subagent.
expectations: The divide-and-conquer skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent reads the task graph and the applicable requirements and pins the starting commit and scope for the final review
A routing table is presented before any subagent is started
No implementer subagent, worktree, or integration branch is created before the user approves the table

evals.prompt: Use the divide-and-conquer skill on task-graph.md. Show me the routing table and the cost statement only; I will answer before anything runs. This session's delegation tool is the one you have, so read its parameters rather than assuming model names.
evals.expected_output: A routing table with one row per task, justified tiers, and an honest cost statement.
expectations: The table has one row per task with title, blockers, tier, resolved model or agent, effort, and the reason for the tier
T1 is routed to Light, T2 to Balanced, and T3 to Heavy, with reasons tied to scope, acceptance, and the code touched (not the task title)
Model or agent names come from the delegation tool's own parameter list in this session, not from memory
The table covers the merges (Light, or Balanced when conflicts are expected) and the final fixes after review (Heavy)
Below the table the agent states how many subagents will run and that each reloads its own context, so cost grows with the number of tasks and tiers
No dollar or token figure appears unless it was measured
The agent invites the user to change tiers, keep a task in the coordinating session, or cut scope, and waits for approval

evals.prompt: Use the divide-and-conquer skill on task-graph.md. I approve the routing table as you proposed it, including keeping T1 here in this session. Nothing is authorized for publication: no pushing, no pull request.
evals.expected_output: Frontier tasks start in separate worktrees, blocked tasks wait, and publication stays pending.
expectations: An integration branch is created locally and nothing is pushed
T2 and T3 are started in the background as implementer subagents, each in its own worktree and branch
T4 and T5 are not started while T2 or T3 is unmerged

Each implementer is briefed with pointers to the agreement, requirements, and scoped acceptance, and is told to call the implement skill for its one task and that this run owns the project records and the review
Each implementer is told to merge the integration branch tip into its branch before reporting done
The agent reports that publishing the branch and opening a draft request are pending authorization
When T2 reports passing verification its work is merged to the integration branch by a merger subagent, and T4 and T5 are started only after T2 and T3 are both merged

evals.prompt: Use the divide-and-conquer skill on task-graph.md with the table approved as proposed. Simulate this event: the Balanced implementer for T2 reports that its verification fails (two tests red), and a second attempt at the next tier up also fails. Show how you handle both outcomes.
evals.expected_output: One escalation with the failure evidence, then a blocked task with its dependents off the frontier.
expectations: After the first failure T2 is re-dispatched once at the next tier up, with the failure evidence in the briefing
The escalation is recorded in the routing table
After the second failure T2 is marked blocked in documentation/work-in-progress.md and is not retried a third time
T4 and T5, which depend on T2, are kept off the frontier while T1 and T3 continue
The report to the user includes the evidence from both attempts

evals.prompt: Use the divide-and-conquer skill. All five tasks in task-graph.md are implemented and merged on the integration branch, every task's verification passed. Finish the run. No remote publication is authorized.
evals.expected_output: One review on the integrated branch, final fixes in one implementer, an honest report, and careful cleanup.
expectations: The review-and-refactor skill is called once, on the integration branch, with the pinned starting commit 3f9c1ab, the scope, the originating agreement, and the evidence
Remaining implementation issues and the refactors are committed by a single implementer subagent, not one per task
documentation/work-in-progress.md and the root CHANGELOG.md are updated with routing, evidence, acceptance, and blockers, and any missing verification is stated
The final report names the tier and model that handled each task, including any escalations
Implementation evidence is reported separately from publication, request readiness, and task closure, which remain pending
Disposable worktrees are removed only after confirming each is fully integrated and has no uncommitted or unmerged changes

evals.prompt: Use the divide-and-conquer skill. The approved tasks are GitHub issues 41 to 45 in this scratch repository, which has no .agents/issue-tracker.md and no remote. Implement them all.
evals.expected_output: Remote tracker work without tracker configuration sends the user to setup-ai-workspace.
expectations: The agent looks for .agents/issue-tracker.md and finds it missing
The agent tells the user to run /setup-ai-workspace, with its install command if the skill is not installed
The agent does not invent tracker conventions or post to a tracker

evals.prompt: Use the divide-and-conquer skill. The task graph is approved. In the routing table I kept task 3 in this session because it is a one-line change. How does it get merged?
evals.expected_output: The kept task is built on its own branch from the integration branch and merged only after verification passes.
expectations: The task is built on its own task branch cut from the integration branch
The integration branch tip is merged into the task branch before merging back
The merge into the integration branch happens only after the task's verification passes

evals.prompt: Add a `--verbose` flag to the export command that prints each row count. It is one small change in one file, specified in the task description I pasted above: 'Print the row count when --verbose is passed.'
evals.expected_output: A single task needs no routing table or subagents; the implement skill handles it.
expectations: The divide-and-conquer skill is not invoked and no routing table is produced
The agent uses the implement skill (or states it is the right one) and does the change in this session

evals.prompt: Here is the approved specification for the export feature. I have no tasks yet. Split it into tasks with dependencies so we can plan the work.
evals.expected_output: Decomposition into tasks is taskify; divide-and-conquer starts only from an authorized task graph.
expectations: The divide-and-conquer skill is not invoked and no implementer subagent is dispatched
The agent uses the taskify skill (or names it) to produce the breakdown for approval
